passages.text: “My spirit is broken; my days are extinguished; the grave awaits me.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks these words.
Job is a man who suffers greatly.
Job says, "My spirit is broken."
Job says, "My days are extinguished."
Job says, "The grave awaits me."
passages.original: רוּחִ֣י חֻ֭בָּלָה יָמַ֥י נִזְעָ֗כוּ קְבָרִ֥ים לִֽי׃

passages.text: Surely mockers surround me, and my eyes must gaze at their rebellion.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in his suffering.
Mockers surround me.
They are with me now.
I see their rebellion.
My eyes look at what they do.
They oppose me openly.
passages.original: אִם־ לֹ֣א הֲ֭תֻלִים עִמָּדִ֑י וּ֝בְהַמְּרוֹתָ֗ם תָּלַ֥ן עֵינִֽי׃

passages.text: Give me, I pray, the pledge You demand. Who else will be my guarantor?
passages.sermon:
Job speaks to God.
Job feels desperate and alone.
Job asks God for help.
Job says, “God, give me the pledge You require.”
Job asks, “Who else will guarantee for me?”
passages.original: שִֽׂימָה־ נָּ֭א עָרְבֵ֣נִי עִמָּ֑ךְ מִֽי ה֝֗וּא לְיָדִ֥י יִתָּקֵֽעַ׃

passages.text: You have closed their minds to understanding; therefore You will not exalt them.
passages.sermon:
God has closed their minds.
They cannot understand.
God will not lift them up.
God will not honor them.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ לִ֭בָּם צָפַ֣נְתָּ מִּשָּׂ֑כֶל עַל־ כֵּ֝֗ן לֹ֣א תְרֹמֵֽם׃

passages.text: If a man denounces his friends for a price, the eyes of his children will fail.
passages.sermon:
A man may betray his friends for money.
He may speak against them to gain a reward.
His children will suffer because of his actions.
His children’s eyes will grow weak and fail.
They will lose hope and strength.
passages.original: לְ֭חֵלֶק יַגִּ֣יד רֵעִ֑ים וְעֵינֵ֖י בָנָ֣יו תִּכְלֶֽנָה׃

passages.text: He has made me a byword among the people, a man in whose face they spit.
passages.sermon:
God has made me a byword among the people.
People use my name as an example of suffering.
People spit in my face.
They show me disrespect.
They treat me with shame.
passages.original: וְֽ֭הִצִּגַנִי לִמְשֹׁ֣ל עַמִּ֑ים וְתֹ֖פֶת לְפָנִ֣ים אֶֽהְיֶֽה׃

passages.text: My eyes have grown dim with grief, and my whole body is but a shadow.
passages.sermon: Job is speaking. Job is a man who suffers greatly. Job feels deep grief.\r\nMy eyes have grown dim from grief.\r\nMy whole body is like a shadow.
passages.original: וַתֵּ֣כַהּ מִכַּ֣עַשׂ עֵינִ֑י וִֽיצֻרַ֖י כַּצֵּ֣ל כֻּלָּֽם׃

passages.text: The upright are appalled at this, and the innocent are stirred against the godless.
passages.sermon:
The upright see this.
They feel shock and horror.
The innocent see the godless.
The innocent rise up against the godless.
passages.original: יָשֹׁ֣מּוּ יְשָׁרִ֣ים עַל־ זֹ֑את וְ֝נָקִ֗י עַל־ חָנֵ֥ף יִתְעֹרָֽר׃

passages.text: Yet a righteous one holds to his way, and the one with clean hands grows stronger.
passages.sermon:
A righteous person holds firmly to his way.
A righteous person does not turn aside.
A person with clean hands becomes stronger.
A person with clean hands gains more strength.
passages.original: וְיֹאחֵ֣ז צַדִּ֣יק דַּרְכּ֑וֹ וּֽטֳהָר־ יָ֝דַ֗יִם יֹסִ֥יף אֹֽמֶץ׃

passages.text: But come back and try again, all of you. For I will not find a wise man among you.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks to his friends.
He tells all of them to return.
He invites them to come again.
He says he will not find a wise man among them.
passages.original: וְֽאוּלָ֗ם כֻּלָּ֣ם תָּ֭שֻׁבוּ וּבֹ֣אוּ נָ֑א וְלֹֽא־ אֶמְצָ֖א בָכֶ֣ם חָכָֽם׃

passages.text: My days have passed; my plans are broken off— even the desires of my heart.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in this passage.
Job is a man who suffers greatly.
He says his life is passing.
He says his days are over.
His plans are destroyed.
His hopes are gone.
His heart’s desires are cut off.
passages.original: יָמַ֣י עָ֭בְרוּ זִמֹּתַ֣י נִתְּק֑וּ מ֖וֹרָשֵׁ֣י לְבָבִֽי׃

passages.text: They have turned night into day, making light seem near in the face of darkness.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks about his suffering.
He says that people have changed night into day.
They make darkness seem like light is near.
They confuse what is dark and what is light.
passages.original: לַ֭יְלָה לְי֣וֹם יָשִׂ֑ימוּ א֝֗וֹר קָר֥וֹב מִפְּנֵי־ חֹֽשֶׁךְ׃

passages.text: If I look for Sheol as my home, if I spread out my bed in darkness, and say to corruption, ‘You are my father,’ and to the worm, ‘My mother,’ or ‘My sister,’ where then is my hope? Who can see any hope for me?
passages.sermon:
Job is speaking.
Job is suffering greatly.
Job feels hopeless.
Job says, “If I look for Sheol as my home, I have made the grave my dwelling place.
I spread out my bed in darkness.
I say to corruption, ‘You are my father.’
I say to the worm, ‘You are my mother and my sister.’
Where is my hope?
Who can see any hope for me?”
passages.original: אִם־ אֲ֭קַוֶּה שְׁא֣וֹל בֵּיתִ֑י בַּ֝חֹ֗שֶׁךְ רִפַּ֥דְתִּי יְצוּעָֽי׃ לַשַּׁ֣חַת קָ֭רָאתִי אָ֣בִי אָ֑תָּה אִמִּ֥י וַ֝אֲחֹתִ֗י לָֽרִמָּֽה׃ וְ֭אַיֵּה אֵפ֣וֹ תִקְוָתִ֑י וְ֝תִקְוָתִ֗י מִ֣י יְשׁוּרֶֽנָּה׃

passages.text: Will it go down to the gates of Sheol? Will we go down together into the dust?”
passages.sermon:
Sheol is the place of the dead.
The gates of Sheol are the entrance to death.
Will hope go down to the gates of Sheol?
Will we go down together into the dust?
The dust is the grave.
This asks if hope will die with us.
passages.original: בַּדֵּ֣י שְׁאֹ֣ל תֵּרַ֑דְנָה אִם־ יַ֖חַד עַל־ עָפָ֣ר נָֽחַת׃ס
